llmsTxt: > Front-end engineer in Nigeria. Open to full-time remote front-end roles, and also to freelance projects. Flexible with working hours.
Generated UI looks finished. That's the problem. I finish it: I check a screen against the source, then I design it.
I use AI tools to build interfaces. I direct the work and I review it, and I check what comes back against the source.
Every claim on the site carries a tag: Check it yourself (a public file, pinned to a commit), Shown (a case study, on sample data) or My word (nothing public backs it).

named.text: My role: the front end of the admin dashboard of ARSIDIDI, an exam-preparation platform.

unnamed.text: My role: the front end of the admin dashboard of an exam-preparation platform.

caseStudies.intro: A dashboard is a thing people act on. So the first question about any card on it is where its number comes from.

lookedFinished.text: Cards, two trend charts and a leaderboard. Every one of them rendered.

itWasnt.text: A card read a field the endpoint never sends. It showed 0.
Both trend charts read keys that weren't in the response. They drew empty frames and raised no error.
A card labelled Resolved showed the Closed figure. The endpoint holds both.
A failed request fell back to 0. An outage looked like a quiet day.

itWasntNote.text: Each has a recorded instance in the working notes for this application. The notes are private, so weigh this one as My word.

owner.text: I compared each card with the response body, field by field.
I changed what the card reads. I did not change the number it shows.
I gave failure its own state, with a retry, so a failure can't pass as a zero.
When a session expired and several requests failed at once, each tried to refresh it. I made them share one refresh and retry in turn.

directed.text: I directed a comparison of each card with the response body, field by field.
The fix changed what the card reads. It did not change the number it shows.
Failure got its own state, with a retry, so a failure can't pass as a zero.
When a session expired and several requests failed at once, each tried to refresh it. They share one refresh and retry in turn.

whatItNeeded.text: A card is finished when it shows the number the source sends, or says it has none. A chart is finished when an empty array and a wrong key look different. A failure is finished when nobody can mistake it for a zero.

stack.text: React, Vite, Tailwind, TanStack Query, React Router, Radix UI, Framer Motion, Recharts and axios.

screens.text: Question bank and groups, bulk import and import history, assets, catalog, answer reviews, custom exams, learning resources, users, roles and permissions, plans and transactions, support tickets, audit logs, and the dashboard.

caseStudies.intro: Lists and filters fail quietly. Nothing breaks. Something just isn't there.

lookedFinished.text: A home page with questions and answers, a filter bar with tabs, and a notification list.

itWasnt.text: The FAQ read the wrong level of the response. It got an empty list, dropped every real question and showed local placeholders instead.
A filter bar had one tab. The subjects behind it were hard-coded to an empty list, so nothing beyond All could appear.
Every notification read as unread, dated Invalid Date. The code read camelCase fields from a response that sends snake_case.

itWasntNote.text: Each has a recorded instance in the working notes for this application. The notes are private, so weigh this one as My word.

owner.text: I read the real response for each list and matched the keys.
I wired the filter to the data it was meant to filter.
I put one mapper between the response and the screen, so one place translates what arrives into what the screen needs.

directed.text: I directed a read of the real response for each list, and a match of the keys.
The filter reads the data it was meant to filter.
One mapper sits between the response and the screen, so one place translates what arrives into what the screen needs.

whatItNeeded.text: A filter is finished when choosing a tab changes what you see. A list is finished when a missing key is an error, not an empty list.

pwa.text: It installs as an app, and its shell works offline. It never caches API responses, so a stale figure can't stand in for a current one. It asks before it applies an update.

stack.text: React, Vite, Tailwind, TanStack Query, React Router, React Hook Form with Zod, KaTeX for mathematics, Radix UI and Framer Motion.

screens.text: Practice, exam mode, custom exams, questions with mathematics, activity history, community, support and settings.

caseStudies.intro: A green build is a statement about the code. It isn't a statement about the page.

lookedFinished.text: The build passed. The type check passed. The accessibility tree showed no errors.

itWasnt.text: The page had no accent colour.
A class syntax from the old framework version compiled to nothing in the new one. The main button rendered as bare text with no fill.
Queried directly, the colour token resolved. On the screen, nothing used it.
A second bug sat behind a passing test. The cake that changes shape as you choose was adding and removing shapes instead of changing them.
A shape that didn't exist last frame can't animate.

owner.text: I looked at the page on an emulated mid-range phone and saw the button had no fill.
I changed every use to the form both versions understand. Then I looked again.
I rewrote the cake so the page keeps the same shapes and transforms them.

directed.text: The audit records that the missing fill was caught by looking at the page on an emulated mid-range phone.
Every use was changed to the form both versions understand, and the page was looked at again.
The cake was rewritten so the page keeps the same shapes and transforms them.

whatItNeeded.text: A green build and an accessibility tree with no errors say the code is well formed. They don't say the page looks right. Someone has to look at it, on a device.

caseStudies.intro: A tool for small businesses that take a deposit before they start: log a booking, create a payment link, track the status.

lookedFinished.text: A booking page that says Deposit paid. A total that adds up.

itWasnt.text: A status is as good as whatever can change it. Anyone who can reach the webhook address can post a payment event.
A total held as decimal naira picks up fractions of a kobo.

itWasntNote.text: These are the two things the code guards against. They aren't defects I found in a running system.

owner.text: A booking can't change to Deposit paid unless the payment provider's signature matches the body. The comparison runs in constant time.
With no key configured, it refuses every event.
A replayed event changes nothing. The update fires once, while the booking is still awaiting its deposit.
If the write fails, it answers 500 so the provider retries.
Money is stored as integer kobo and formatted when a person reads it.

directed.text: A booking can't change to Deposit paid unless the payment provider's signature matches the body. The comparison runs in constant time.
With no key configured, it refuses every event.
A replayed event changes nothing. The update fires once, while the booking is still awaiting its deposit.
If the write fails, it answers 500 so the provider retries.
Money is stored as integer kobo and formatted when a person reads it.

whatItNeeded.text: A status is finished when one thing can change it: a signed event. Money is finished when it is a whole number until someone reads it.

tests.text: Its tests cover a correct signature, a wrong one, a tampered body, a missing header, a missing key and a replayed event.

shortEntries.title: PizzaPoint
shortEntries.text: A demo ordering site. Its README has a section called "What's genuinely not done". The server decides what each item costs. The browser never does. Built with an AI assistant, and the commit history shows it.

text.owner: Before I trust a screen, I open the response. I compare the keys the component reads with the keys that arrive, and each label with its field. Then I run the screen.
text.directed: Before I trust a screen, I have it checked against the response: the keys it reads against the keys that arrive, each label against its field. Then I read the result and decide what stays.

items.title: I write the spec down.
items.text: I write down what a screen must do and what it must never do, before it is built. A rule that is written down can be checked.

items.title: I audit, and I list what I didn't check.
items.text: Each claim in an audit is marked checked, partly checked or not checked. The list of what I didn't check goes in the same file.

items.title: I design the empty, loading and error states.
items.text: The full state is the easy one. The dashboard above gives the other three their own design, and so does this page.
